To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

emotional distress contributes most significantly to drug and alcohol use among adolescents, and that gender, internal resources and external resources contribute differentially to drug and alcohol abuse.
emotional distress is the most important predictor of drug use, and gender, internal and external resources, emotional maturity, and age contribute differentially to drug and alcohol use.
Among urban Israeli Jewish adolescents, the most significant predictors of alcohol and drug use are emotional distress and age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between internal and external resources and emotional distress to drug and alcohol use among adolescents.
the contribution of selected background, internal, and external resources, and emotional distress to the use of alcohol and drugs among urban adolescents in Israel.
the contribution of selected variables to the use of alcohol and drugs among adolescents in Israel and the differences in the contribution of these variables to the use and the type of drug use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most significant predictor of both drug and alcohol use is emotional distress.
the contribution of the variables to alcohol and drug abuse is complex and multifaceted.
the contribution of the variables to alcohol and drug consumption is complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
emotional distress contributes most strongly to alcohol and drug problems, and that the contribution of gender, internal resources, external resources, and age are less significant.
emotional distress and external resources contribute to the use of drugs and alcohol.
emotional distress contributes to alcohol and drug consumption among adolescents and that the contribution of external resources is more specific to alcohol consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contribution of emotional distress to alcohol or drug use among adolescents can be mediated by the interaction with internal resources, which can also contribute directly.
emotional distress, internal resources, external resources and age contribute differentially to alcohol use and drug use.
emotional distress and the interaction of emotional distress with one's sense (of mastery) are the strongest contributors to alcohol and drug abuse among adolescents.
